turns.patient_response: I can’t stop fixating on how awful I look on camera and in photos, and it’s starting to affect my work and social life. It has just gotten to the point where it's really overwhelming, so a close friend encouraged me to come speak with someone.

turns.patient_response: It is definitely about how I look, not a general fear of socializing. I am terrified that people will notice my dark circles and bloated face and judge me for looking exhausted or sloppy, especially after some coworkers made comments about me looking "tired" on screen. If my appearance isn't the focus, I don't feel anxious at all.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses intense anxiety and preoccupation regarding perceived flaws in their physical appearance, specifically dark circles and a bloated face, fearing judgment from others.

turns.patient_response: To me, it feels incredibly real and obvious, and I'm constantly convinced that everyone is judging me for looking exhausted and sloppy. Even though my friends tell me they don't notice anything wrong when I ask them, I still can't stop replaying the images in my head. Because of that, it is really hard for me to believe that I might just be exaggerating it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient is preoccupied with looking 'exhausted and sloppy,' which they perceive as highly obvious, despite friends stating they do not notice anything wrong.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient engages in repetitive appearance-related behaviors, specifically seeking reassurance by asking friends if they notice anything wrong and mentally replaying images of themselves.

turns.patient_response: Yes, absolutely. Before any video call or social event, I spend 30 to 40 minutes adjusting the lighting, testing angles, and redoing my makeup to hide my puffy face and eye bags. During the calls, I constantly check my camera preview box, and afterward, I zoom in on tagged photos and repeatedly ask my friends if I looked that bad.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient expresses preoccupation with perceived flaws in her physical appearance, specifically her 'puffy face and eye bags.'
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to her appearance concerns, including excessive camouflaging (makeup, lighting, angles), mirror checking (checking camera preview, zooming in on photos), and reassurance seeking (asking friends if she looked bad).

turns.patient_response: To be honest, at my deepest level, it feels completely real and obvious, and there are times when I am absolutely certain no one could convince me otherwise. Even when my friends reassure me that they don't notice anything, I'm convinced they're just being polite to spare my feelings. I just can't shake the belief that everyone else must secretly see how exhausted and sloppy I look.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes a persistent, unshakeable belief that they look 'exhausted and sloppy' despite reassurance from friends who do not notice these appearance flaws.
